title: filelock ReadWriteLock: SQLite reopens the lock database by name, so a planted symlink or journal file makes the lock…
description: CVE-2026-112940 affects the filelock library's ReadWriteLock and AsyncReadWriteLock components that use SQLite for locking. On Linux systems with /proc mounted, SQLite reopens lock database files by name, following symlinks and acting on side files such as -journal, -wal, and -shm. A local attacker with write access to the directory containing the lock database can exploit this to cause the lock user to overwrite or unlink files with the lock user's privileges. This requires the directory to be writable without the sticky bit, such as a 0777 or group-writable directory without sticky bit. The vulnerability is present in filelock versions 3.20.4 through 4.2.0, with the /proc/self/fd redirect introduced in 4.0.9 and side-file variants since 3.20.4. The issue can cause high integrity and availability impact but no confidentiality loss. A fix is available in version 1.18.4 of the affected product pipx.
